text:
Maya R: Noticed spikes of stalled spans in the OTLP exporter from the API gateway this morning. gRPC streams are getting stuck during high tail latency and we're seeing batch queues grow.

Ian S: Is this only gRPC? Any stack dumps or errors?

Maya R: Mostly gRPC. Logs show repeated timeouts and http2 transport errors. Snippet:
```
2026-03-05T09:07:14Z warn exporter/otlp: send timeout, retrying (attempt=2)
2026-03-05T09:07:14Z error grpc: transport: http2Client.notifyError got notified that the client transport was broken
```
Queue depth on the batching layer jumped from ~200 to 4k.

Priya K: Do exporters point at our relay or directly to vendor? If relay, can we switch protocol there? HTTP might avoid single-stream stalls.

Maya R: All tenants go through the relay. Relay supports both otlp-grpc and otlp-http/protobuf. My proposal: keep gRPC as default for perf but add automatic protocol fallback to HTTP when gRPC shows repeated failures. Also tighten retries/backoff and add per-tenant circuit breakers.

Alex T: OK. We need concrete defaults so infra and SDKs behave predictably. How many retries and what backoff curve?

Maya R: Draft config (per-tenant overrideable):
```
exporter:
  protocol: grpc
  timeout_ms: 8000
  max_retries: 3
  backoff:
    initial_ms: 250
    multiplier: 2.0
    max_ms: 4000
    jitter: 0.20
  failover:
    enabled: true
    to_protocol: http_protobuf
    consecutive_failures: 3
    cooldown_ms: 45000
  buffer_capacity_spans: 2000  # default for gateway
  retention_ms: 180000
```
If gRPC fails 3 consecutive export attempts, switch to HTTP for 45s. During failover we continue flushing buffered batches via HTTP.

Ian S: Add a capped jitter and max_backoff for safety (you already have max_ms). Also add a circuit-breaker that trips if buffer > 75% for > 30s and then stop retrying (emit metric + drop spans). We must avoid increasing pressure on the relay/vendor.

Priya K: Agree. From UX side we need console signals: per-tenant exporter_status, failover_count, dropped_spans, and a timeline. Also tag outgoing span metadata with export_path and export_result so downstream metrics and debug traces show what happened.

Maya R: Proposed additional tags on exported telemetry: exported_via: grpc|http, export_outcome: ok|retry|dropped, export_error: <short-code>. And metrics to push to metrics pipeline:
- exporter_export_attempts{protocol,tenant}
- exporter_export_successes{protocol,tenant}
- exporter_export_failures{protocol,tenant,reason}
- exporter_queue_length{tenant}
- exporter_failover_events{tenant}

Observability Bot: Alert: exporter_failover_events spiked for tenant=vertex-ml (18 events) at 2026-03-05T09:07:22Z.

Alex T: Implementation notes:
- Make exporter a small async state machine. No blocking threads in request path.
- Use a bounded worker pool to flush batches; if pool is exhausted, increment a dropped_spans metric and drop oldest batches.
- Keep per-tenant state isolated to avoid noisy-neighbor propagation.

Ian S: Add an active health probe for relay endpoints. If gRPC health-check fails twice (interval 10s), proactively prefer HTTP until health returns. Health-checks should be non-blocking and low-overhead.

Priya K: Console UX: show a soft banner for tenants currently in failover, clickable timeline, and manual controls to force failover/fallback. Also include a recommended retention window for span buffers so ops can tune for their SLAs.

Maya R: Action items:
- Maya R: implement exporter config parsing, fallback state machine, and metrics emission. Target: PR in 6 days.
- Ian S: design and add per-tenant circuit-breaker thresholds + health-check probe. Target: PR in 3 days.
- Priya K: console telemetry changes, banner and manual override UI. Target: PR in 9 days.
- Alex T: worker pool + buffer semantics and unit/integration tests. Target: PR in 5 days.

DevOps Bot: CI started for branch maya/otlp-fallback (build 2371) -> https://ci.redwood.example/builds/2371

Maya R: I'll drop an RFC in #eng-platform with the YAML defaults and a short simulation of failure modes this afternoon. Any objections to these numbers? We can tune per-product.

Alex T: Lower default buffer for gateway makes sense (2000). Services with longer lifecycles can raise to 10000. Also consider a maximum global buffer cap to bound memory.

Ian S: +1 on global cap. Also make retention_ms configurable so we don't keep spans indefinitely when downstream is degraded.

Priya K: When we roll this out, let's do a canary in staging for 24h and monitor exporter_failover_rate and dropped_spans before wider rollout.

Maya R: Sounds good. I'll include canary plan in RFC and link metrics dashboards.

Observability Bot: Note: recording rule exporter_failover_rate increased for env=staging after deploy; monitoring for 24h.

Ian S: One more: add a debug endpoint that returns exporter state for a tenant (current protocol, consecutive_failures, buffer_size) gated by admin auth.

Maya R: Good suggestion, will add.

Priya K: Thanks everyone. If no further objections I'll merge RFC after small edits and schedule the canary.

Ian S: +1
